passage: My name is Anand. Last spring my manager Pooja asked me to change the supplier's invoice date so the payment would look on time. She said it kindly, as if it were nothing. My face went warm. I said, "Can you send me that in an email, so I have it clear?" She laughed and told me not to be so formal. I said I would still prefer it in writing. She went quiet. Two teammates, Rohit and Zara, kept their eyes on their screens. That evening I emailed the finance controller a plain question about the correct procedure. No drama. Pooja did not speak to me for two days, and then she nodded at me in the lift.

qa.q: What did Pooja ask Anand to change?
qa.a: Pooja asked Anand to change the supplier's invoice date.

qa.q: What was Anand feeling when asking for the request in writing?
qa.a: Anand felt nervous, with a warm face, but resolved; the calm repetition "in writing" shows Anand was determined not to be swept along.

qa.q: Which steps did Anand use to decline without a fight?
qa.a: Anand asked for the instruction in writing and then sent a plain question about the correct procedure to the finance controller, using the proper channel instead of arguing.

qa.q: How might Pooja have felt when Anand asked for the request in writing?
qa.a: Pooja may have felt caught out or irritated; going quiet and not speaking for two days suggests discomfort before the nod in the lift.

grounding: An adult declines an improper instruction calmly, asks for it in writing and uses a proper channel, knowing orders do not remove responsibility.

passage: Note from the department head, Lalit. On Wednesday a director told Gargi, in front of the analysis team, to remove a warning line from the quarterly report. Gargi said calmly, "I can do that if you send the instruction in writing, and I would like the compliance team to see the report first." The room went silent. Two analysts looked at me. The director walked out. I stood by Gargi's request, and that afternoon I passed the matter to compliance myself and told the analysts this is how a query should be handled. Gargi did not raise her voice once.

qa.q: What did the director tell Gargi to remove from the report?
qa.a: The director told Gargi to remove a warning line from the quarterly report.

qa.q: What does Gargi's calm request for the instruction in writing suggest about how Gargi feels?
qa.a: It suggests Gargi feels steady and sure of the proper route, without needing to win or accuse anyone, since Gargi did not raise a voice once.

qa.q: What turning point in Lalit's response backed Gargi up?
qa.a: Lalit stood by the request and passed the matter to compliance that afternoon, which showed the analysts the proper channel in action.

qa.q: What might the two analysts who looked at Lalit have been feeling?
qa.a: They may have felt tense and unsure, checking whether the head would support Gargi or the director; they were waiting to see what was safe.

grounding: An adult refuses an improper instruction calmly, asks for it in writing and uses proper channels, a case of personal responsibility surviving orders.

passage:
Tuesday night
Sabina ma'am called me in at five. The pipe batch for the housing project failed the pressure test by a small margin. She wants me to sign it off. “It's within tolerance, Shankar. Everyone rounds.”
Rakesh and Imtiaz were in the cabin. They stayed silent.
I said, calmly I think, “Ma'am, I can't sign a failed test. If you want it passed, please send me the instruction in writing.” She went quiet. Then she said she'd think about it.
I didn't wait. At six I emailed the quality head with the test sheet attached. He replied by seven: batch on hold, retest tomorrow, and he'll speak to ma'am himself.
People will live in those flats. My signature is mine, whoever tells me to use it.

qa.q: Who did Shankar email at six?
qa.a: He emailed the quality head with the test sheet attached.

qa.q: What was Shankar feeling when he refused?
qa.a: Shankar felt calm but firm, and later settled, because the signature belongs to Shankar whoever gives the order.

qa.q: Which of Shankar's steps made the refusal strong?
qa.a: Shankar asked for the order in writing and used the proper channel by emailing the quality head with evidence, so it wasn't just his word.

qa.q: What would change for Rakesh and Imtiaz after Shankar's refusal?
qa.a: They saw someone say no calmly, which may make it easier for them to speak up next time.

grounding: Shows an engineer calmly declining an improper sign-off, asking for it in writing and going to the proper channel.

passage:
Lavanya: Yamini, reject the candidate from this morning. The one who mentioned she's expecting.
Yamini: She scored highest on the test. What reason should I record?
Lavanya: Just say culture fit. We can't have someone on leave in three months.
Yamini: I'm not comfortable doing that. Could you please send the instruction by email?
Lavanya: Seriously? It's a small thing.
Yamini: I understand the pressure on the team. But I can't record a false reason.
Later.
Yamini: Mr Dsouza, I need guidance on a hiring instruction I've been given. I've attached the chat. I haven't acted on it.
Mr Dsouza: Thank you for flagging this. Please hold the decision. I'll speak with Lavanya today. You won't be penalised for raising it.
Yamini: Thank you 🙏

qa.q: What reason did Lavanya want recorded?
qa.a: She wanted "culture fit" recorded as the reason.

qa.q: How was Yamini feeling when she asked for the instruction by email?
qa.a: Yamini felt uncomfortable and under pressure, but calm and steady enough to ask for it in writing.

qa.q: What makes Yamini's response a good model?
qa.a: Yamini refused calmly, asked for the order in writing and took it to Mr Dsouza with evidence, without acting on it.

qa.q: How might the candidate be affected by Yamini's choice?
qa.a: She has a fair chance at the job she earned by scoring highest, instead of being rejected unfairly without knowing why.

grounding: Shows an employee calmly declining an unethical hiring instruction, asking for it in writing and using the proper channel.

passage:
In the block office at Sirsa, the ration list for the village was due by evening. Mohit, the supervisor, pushed a paper across Zainab's desk.
“Remove these three families. They're making trouble with the sarpanch.”
The other two clerks bent over their files. Outside, a queue of farmers waited on the bench.
Zainab read the names. All three families had valid cards, she knew. “Sir, they're eligible. I can't remove them without a reason. Please give me the order in writing.”
Mohit laughed. “In writing? For this?”
“Yes, sir.”
He took the paper back and left. Zainab wrote a short note to the Block Development Officer and handed it in before four. The BDO read it, called Mohit in, and the three names stayed.

qa.q: How many families was Zainab told to remove?
qa.a: She was told to remove three families.

qa.q: How did Zainab feel when Mohit laughed?
qa.a: She seemed calm and steady; she simply said "Yes, sir" without getting angry or backing down.

qa.q: Why did Zainab write to the Block Development Officer?
qa.a: Using the proper channel meant the improper order was checked by someone above Mohit, and it protected both the families and Zainab.

qa.q: How might the three families have been affected if Zainab had obeyed?
qa.a: They would have lost their ration without any fair reason, just for disagreeing with the sarpanch.

grounding: Shows a clerk calmly declining an improper order, asking for it in writing and using the proper channel.

passage:
The site office in Leeds smelled of wet boots and coffee. Declan, the site manager, slid the inspection sheet across to Amara. "Just tick the scaffold check for level three and sign. We'll do it properly Monday. The client's here at nine."
Ines and two labourers by the kettle went quiet.
Amara read the sheet twice. "I can't sign that it's been checked when it hasn't," she said evenly. "If you want it logged this way, could you put the instruction in an email? Then I'll take it to the safety officer."
Declan's jaw tightened. "You're making a big deal of this."
"I'm not trying to. I'll do the check myself right now, if someone comes with me."
Ines put her mug down. "I'll come."
The check took forty minutes. One clamp was loose. Declan never sent the email. At nine, he walked the client round level two instead.

qa.q: How long did the scaffold check take?
qa.a: The check took forty minutes.

qa.q: How can you tell Amara felt steady rather than defiant?
qa.a: Amara spoke evenly, offered another way and did the check herself, which suggests she felt calm and determined, even if tense under Declan's pressure.

qa.q: Which parts of Amara's response made it wise, not just stubborn?
qa.a: She refused only the false signature, asked for the order in writing, named the safety officer as the channel and offered to fix the real problem at once.

qa.q: How might Declan see Amara's refusal?
qa.a: Declan seems irritated and pressured by the client visit, but steering the client away from level three suggests he knew the check mattered.

grounding: Shows an adult calmly refusing an improper instruction, asking for it in writing and using the proper safety channel, accepting that orders do not remove her own responsibility.
